Park Chung Hee: President of South Korea from 1963 to 1979.
He became king in 2013 when his father abdicated for health reasons, and his eldest daughter, Princess Elisabeth, is now first in line to succeed him — who is he?
Philippe of Belgium: King of the Belgians since 2013.
Known in Hebrew as 'praises,' this anthology of 150 religious hymns is divided into five sections each closing with a doxology — which book of the Bible is it?
Psalms: Book of sacred songs in the Hebrew Bible.
A Bosnian Serb commander of the Army of Republika Srpska during the Yugoslav Wars, he's now serving a life sentence in The Hague for genocide and crimes against humanity — who is he?
This American author built a personal-finance empire around his bestselling Rich Dad Poor Dad book series, even as one of his companies filed for bankruptcy in 2012 — who is he?
Robert Kiyosaki: American finance author and investor (born 1947)
An Iraqi politician who served as the fifth president from 1979 until his overthrow in 2003 during the US-led invasion, previously a vice president and prime minister—who was he?
Saddam Hussein: President of Iraq from 1979 to 2003. The policies and ideologies he championed are collectively known as Saddamism, a right-wing variant of Ba'athism.
This Sanskrit term, meaning 'wandering' or 'running around in circles,' describes the ongoing cycle of life, death, and rebirth central to Indian religious philosophy — what is it called?
Saṃsāra: Indian concept of the cyclical process of death and rebirth.
After a stint as a teacher, this man rose to become the first democratically elected president of Nigeria when the military handed over power in 1979, launching the Second Republic — who was he?
Shehu Shagari: President of Nigeria from 1979 to 1983.
Born in Požarevac and a law graduate of Belgrade, he became the first sitting head of state ever charged with war crimes — which Serbian president, overthrown in 2000?
Slobodan Milošević: Yugoslav and Serbian politician (1941–2006)
Serving as Saudi Arabia's defense minister for nearly five decades, which royal became Crown Prince in 2005 and held the title until his death in 2011?
Sultan bin Abdulaziz: Saudi royal and politician (1925–2011)
Second only to Cameroon's leader in tenure among non-royal heads of state, this president has ruled Equatorial Guinea since ousting his uncle in a 1979 coup — who is he?
Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo: Dictator of Equatorial Guinea since 1979. Obiang was Chairperson of the African Union from 2011 to 2012.

The third shōgun of a ruling dynasty, this Japanese leader closed the country's borders to Europeans and persecuted Christians during his 1623-1651 reign, a policy that lasted over two centuries — who is he?
Tokugawa Iemitsu: Japanese Samurai, Daimyo and Military leader of Japan from 1623 to 1651.
With Merlin's magic making him look like his rival Gorlois, this legendary British king slept with Lady Igraine and fathered a certain 'once and future king' — who was he?
Uther Pendragon: Father of King Arthur in Arthurian legend.
As Vice Chair of Russia's State Duma from a liberal-leaning party, he ran in the 2024 presidential election calling for peace negotiations 'without a rollback' — who is he?
Among Queen Victoria's 42 grandchildren he was the eldest, yet he'd preside over the end of his dynasty's 400-year grip on Prussia when he abdicated in 1918 — which last German Emperor?
Wilhelm II: German Emperor from 1888 to 1918.
This Indian politician, who leads the Andhra Pradesh unit of the Congress party, is the daughter of a former chief minister and younger sister of another prominent state politician — who is she?
This authoritarian ruler seized Tunisia's presidency in a bloodless 1987 coup by declaring his predecessor incompetent, then fled to Saudi Arabia when revolution toppled him in 2011 — who was he?
Zine El Abidine Ben Ali: President of Tunisia from 1987 to 2011.
Which of these people was born first?
Thomas Carlyle (born 1795) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these people was born first?
Levi Strauss (born 1829) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these was born first?
John Ray (born 1627) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these was founded earliest?
Lisp (programming language) (founded 1958) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below is best known as an astronomer?
Toghon Temür is an astronomer. Toghon Temür acceded to the throne in 1333 after years of succession disputes following his father's death.
Which of these is a mathematician?
Euclid is a mathematician. Euclid (Ancient Greek: Εὐκλείδης; fl. 300 BC) was an ancient Greek mathematician active as a geometer and logician.
What is the atomic number of Antimony?
Antimony is a chemical element with the symbol Sb (from Latin stibium) and atomic number 51.
What is the atomic number of Chromium?
Chromium is a chemical element; it has symbol Cr and atomic number 24.
In what year was Dolph Lundgren born?
Dolph Lundgren: Hans "Dolph" Lundgren (Swedish: [ˈdɔlːf ˈlɵ̌nːdɡreːn]; born 3 November 1957) is a Swedish-American actor, filmmaker, and martial artist.
In what year was Peng Liyuan born?
Peng Liyuan: Peng also sang the theme songs of several popular TV series, such as The Water Margin (1998).
In what year was Euclid born?
Euclid: Euclid (Ancient Greek: Εὐκλείδης; fl. 300 BC) was an ancient Greek mathematician active as a geometer and logician.
In what year did Pope Benedict XVI die?
Pope Benedict XVI: Following his resignation, he chose to be known as "pope emeritus", a title he held until his death on 31 December 2022.
In what year did Mileva Marić die?
Mileva Marić: Marić and Einstein were study colleagues and lovers, and had a daughter Lieserl in 1902, who likely died of scarlet fever at one and a half years old.
In what year was Theobroma cacao discovered?
Theobroma cacao (cacao tree or cocoa tree) is a small (6–12 m (20–39 ft) tall) evergreen tree in the Malvaceae family.
Mikoyan MiG-31: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG. The MiG-31 is the fastest known operational combat aircraft, with a top speed around 3,000 km/h (1,600 knots).
Which company manufactures CAC/PAC JF-17 Thunder?
CAC/PAC JF-17 Thunder: Chengdu Aircraft Industry Group. The JF-17 can be used for multiple roles, including interception, ground attack, anti-ship, and aerial reconnaissance.
In which country did the CAC/PAC JF-17 Thunder take place?
CAC/PAC JF-17 Thunder: People's Republic of China. The JF-17 can be used for multiple roles, including interception, ground attack, anti-ship, and aerial reconnaissance.
Who is credited with discovering Darmstadtium?
GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research
Darmstadtium: GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research. Darmstadtium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Ds and atomic number 110.
Who is credited with discovering 2 Pallas?
2 Pallas: Heinrich Wilhelm Olbers. Pallas (minor-planet designation: 2 Pallas) is the third-largest asteroid in the Solar System by volume and mass.
Who is credited with discovering Multiple sclerosis?
Multiple sclerosis: Jean-Martin Charcot. It is a type of demyelinating disease, where the nervous system's ability to transmit signals is damaged.
One of the very few semiaquatic vipers in the world, which venomous pit viper native to the southeastern United States is often found coiled near slow-moving lakes, streams, and marshes?
Agkistrodon piscivorus is a species of venomous snake, a pit viper in the subfamily Crotalinae of the family Viperidae.
This group of large, semiaquatic boas native to tropical South America includes the green species, among the largest snakes on Earth — name the group?
Anaconda are a group of large boas of the genus Eunectes.
More than 500 orb-weaving spider species, including the familiar garden spider, belong to this genus first classified in 1757 — which genus?
Araneus is a genus of common orb-weaving spiders with more than 500 species, among which are the European garden spider and the barn spider.
Derived from a particular acid, this class of depressant drugs once treated anxiety and insomnia, but their overdose risk got them largely replaced by benzodiazepines and 'Z-drugs' — what are they?
Barbiturate are a class of depressant drugs that are chemically derived from barbituric acid.
This brittle, silvery-white post-transition metal can develop a vividly iridescent, rainbow-colored surface from thin-film oxidation when heated. What element is it?
Bismuth is a chemical element; it has symbol Bi and atomic number 83.
This outdated 19th-century term for what's now called acute or chronic nephritis was marked by swelling and albumin showing up in the urine — what was it called?
Bright's disease is a historical classification of kidney diseases that are described in modern medicine as acute or chronic nephritis.
Bordered by Aquila, Sagittarius, and Aquarius in the sky's watery region, this half-goat, half-fish zodiac figure is the tiniest of the twelve — which constellation?
Capricornus is one of the constellations of the zodiac.
This genus of deciduous trees and shrubs in the beech family, native to the temperate Northern Hemisphere, gives its name to a widely eaten edible nut it produces — what's this tree (and nut) called?
Chestnut are the deciduous trees and shrubs in the genus Castanea, in the beech family Fagaceae.

Native to Australasia and ranging from the Philippines to the Solomon Islands, these 21 parrot species are recognizable by their prominent crests and curved bills, with plumage that's mostly white, grey, or black — name the group?
Cockatoo is any of the 21 species of parrots belonging to the family Cacatuidae, the only family in the superfamily Cacatuoidea, native to Australasia.

This family of fifteen tall, long-necked bird species mostly wears muted gray-and-white plumage with a patch of bare red skin on the face — except for one crowned genus that stands out — what bird is it?
Crane (bird) are a type of large bird with long legs and necks in the biological family Gruidae of the order Gruiformes.
When insulin runs short, the body burns fat into acidic ketones, causing deep gasping breaths and fruity-smelling breath in this potentially life-threatening emergency — what is it?
Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is a potentially life-threatening acute complication of diabetes mellitus.
This social science examines the production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services, analyzing everything from individual agents to entire economies. What discipline is this?
Economics is a social science that studies the production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services.

A German Jew who fled the Nazi regime for the United States, this social psychologist and psychoanalyst co-founded a New York psychiatric institute and was associated with the Frankfurt School of critical theory — who is he?
Erich Fromm (March 23, 1900 - March 18, 1980) was a German-American social psychologist, psychoanalyst, sociologist, humanistic philosopher, and democratic socialist.
This plant genus of roughly 850 species includes woody trees, vines, and epiphytes native to the tropics, though only two species are widely cultivated for their sweet fruit — what genus is it?
Ficus (or) is a genus of about 850 species of woody trees, shrubs, vines, epiphytes and hemiepiphytes in the family Moraceae.

This Austrian engineer founded a firearms company in 1963; when his first pistol entered Austrian service in 1982, its famous model number referred to his 17th patent, not the rounds it held — who is he?
Prince Carl Philip, Duke of Värmland
Gaston Glock (19 July 1929 - 27 December 2023) was an Austrian engineer and businessman.

Five species of this group of plants — rice, wheat, maize, barley, and sugar cane — together cover 46 percent of the world's arable land, alongside two related families, sedges and rushes. What kind of plant is this?
Grass refers to various families of plants.
Which 19th-century American economist's wildly popular treatise Progress and Poverty argued that a single tax on the value of land could build a more just and productive society?
Henry George (September 2, 1839 - October 29, 1897) was an American political economist, social philosopher and journalist.
A body-temperature emergency defined as a reading above 104°F, this condition kills roughly half a million people annually and is most commonly triggered by heat stroke — what is it called?
Hyperthermia is a condition in which an individual's body temperature is elevated beyond normal due to failed thermoregulation.
This medical condition describes a restricted blood supply to tissue or an organ, starving cells of the oxygen they need and often resulting from a blocked or narrowed vessel — what is it called?
Ischemia is a restriction in blood supply to any tissue, muscle group, or organ of the body.

Nicknamed 'Marvellous Merchiston,' this Scottish laird and mathematician popularised the decimal point and invented a set of calculating 'bones' — but he's best known for discovering what underlies the slide rule. Who was he?
John Napier (Latinized as Ioannes Neper; 1 February 1550 - 4 April 1617), nicknamed Marvellous Merchiston, was a Scottish landowner known as a mathematician, physicist and astronomer.
When the natural curve of the thoracic spine exceeds about 45 degrees, doctors give this excessive rounding of the upper back a name rooted in the Greek word for 'hump' — what is it?
Kyphosis (from Greek (kyphos) 'hump') is an abnormally excessive convex curvature of the spine as it occurs in the thoracic and sacral regions.
Sociable for a big cat and more active by day than its relatives, this savannah hunter is so sexually dimorphic that only the males grow a sweeping mane. Which animal?
Lion (Panthera leo) is a large cat of the genus Panthera, currently ranging only in Sub-Saharan Africa and India.

This German sexologist founded the Scientific-Humanitarian Committee, which carried out what's been called the first advocacy for homosexual and transgender rights — before the Nazis stripped his citizenship in 1933. Who was he?
Magnus Hirschfeld (14 May 1868 - 14 May 1935) was a German physician, sexologist, and LGBTQ advocate whose German citizenship was revoked in 1933 by the Nazi government.
First isolated from a cow's pineal gland in 1958 because it could lighten the skin of frogs, this nighttime hormone went on to become famous for governing the sleep-wake cycle — what is it?
Melatonin is a natural compound produced by various organisms, including bacteria and eukaryotes.
This small, subterranean mammal has velvety fur, tiny eyes, and short powerful forelimbs with oversized paws built for constant digging — what animal is it?

It's the inherent character of the universe as a whole — the laws, elements, and phenomena of the physical world, including life itself — even though humans are often spoken of as somehow apart from it. What is it?
Nature is an inherent character or constitution, particularly of the ecosphere or the universe as a whole.
This family of three long, ribbon-like pelagic fish species includes the longest bony fish alive, stretching up to about 8 meters, yet rarely seen by humans — what fish is it?
Oarfish are the three species of large and extremely long pelagic lampriform fish belonging to the small family Regalecidae.
Its name comes from the Greek for "from everywhere" because it turns up in nearly all foods — and this B vitamin lets animals build coenzyme A for energy. Which vitamin is it?
Pantothenic acid (vitamin B5) is a B vitamin and an essential nutrient.
This Belgian-British microbiologist helped discover the Ebola virus in 1976 and led the fight against that first recorded outbreak before becoming a pioneering AIDS researcher — who is he?
Peter Piot (born 17 February 1949) is a Belgian-British microbiologist known for his research into Ebola and AIDS.
Which silvery-white precious metal carries the symbol Pt, leads group 10 of the periodic table, and is far rarer in Earth's crust than its glittering cousins?
Platinum is a chemical element; it has symbol Pt and atomic number 78.
This viscous, nearly odorless liquid with a faintly sweet taste is classified as a diol and is approved by the FDA as a safe food additive — what compound is it?
Propylene glycol (IUPAC name: propane-1,2-diol) is a viscous, colorless liquid.
This German centre-back developed through Hertha BSC's youth ranks before winning many honors at Bayern Munich, following a season at Manchester City. Who is he?
Rattus is a genus of muroid rodents, all typically called rats.

Known by folk names like knotberry and lowbush salmonberry, this amber fruit structurally similar to a blackberry thrives in Arctic tundra and boreal forest but isn't farmed commercially — which species?
Rubus chamaemorus (also known as cloudberry) is a species of flowering plant in the rose family, Rosaceae.
Most episodes of this brain-activity disruption last under two minutes and leave the person confused or fatigued afterward, but one lasting over five minutes is a medical emergency — what is it?
Seizure is a sudden disruption of brain activity caused by excessive, synchronized neuronal firing that results in changes in behavior.
With symbol Na from the Neo-Latin 'natrium' and a single stable isotope, this reactive metal sits in group 1 and is found in minerals like halite and feldspar — what is it?
Sodium is a chemical element; it has symbol Na (from Neo-Latin natrium) and atomic number 11.
A small Eurasian mustelid that turns brilliant white in winter, this animal's coat — known as ermine — once draped Catholic monarchs and the Infant Jesus of Prague — what is it?
Stoat (Mustela erminea), also known as the Eurasian ermine or ermine, is a species of mustelid native to Eurasia and the northern regions of North America.
A mathematics prodigy who abandoned academia in 1969 for a reclusive primitive life, he later mailed bombs over 17 years and penned a 35,000-word manifesto against modern technology — who was he?
Ted Kaczynski (k-; May 22, 1942 - June 10, 2023), also known as the Unabomber, was an American mathematician and domestic terrorist.
This metric unit of mass equals exactly 1,000 kilograms — about 2,204.6 pounds — and is technically identical to the SI unit called the megagram. What is it?
Tonne (or; symbol: t) is a unit of mass equal to 1,000 kilograms.
At just 26, this Soviet cosmonaut became the first woman in space, orbiting Earth 48 times solo aboard Vostok 6 in 1963. Who is she?
Valentina Tereshkova (born 6 March 1937) is a Russian engineer, politician, and former Soviet cosmonaut.

Dubbed the "father of English geology," this man created the first detailed geological map of an entire country — yet his humble background got him snubbed by scientists and even landed him in debtors' prison. Who was he?
William Smith (geologist) (23 March 1769 - 28 August 1839) was an English geologist, credited with creating the first detailed, nationwide geological map of any country.
A legendary Heian-era court diviner and astrologer, this figure lived 84 years free of illness, fueling belief in mystical powers — a Kyoto shrine bears his name today. Who is he?
A shortened-fuselage version of a popular narrow-body jetliner family, this aircraft entered service with Swissair in April 1996 and carries up to 156 passengers — which model?
Airbus A319: Airliner, shortened variant of the A320 family.
Sold under the brand name Xanax, this fast-acting benzodiazepine is most often prescribed for panic disorder and generalized anxiety — what drug is it?
Alprazolam: Benzodiazepine medication. Alprazolam is most commonly prescribed in the management of anxiety disorders, especially panic disorder and generalized anxiety disorder (GAD).
Commonly called windflowers, which genus of the buttercup family is native to every continent except Australia, New Zealand, and Antarctica?
Anemone: Genus of flowering plants in the family Ranunculaceae.
Named for a mythological weaver transformed into a spider, which eight-legged class of arthropods includes scorpions, ticks, and mites?
Arachnid: Class of arthropods. The term is derived from the Greek word ἀράχνη (aráchnē, 'spider'), from the myth of the hubristic human weaver Arachne, who was turned into a spider.
This ocean giant, recorded at up to 680 kg, has vanished from the Black Sea but still roams the Mediterranean and both sides of another major ocean — which fish?
Atlantic bluefin tuna: Species of fish. The Atlantic bluefin tuna (Thunnus thynnus) is a species of tuna in the family Scombridae.

Developed in the 18th century by an English clergyman and, independently, by Pierre-Simon Laplace, this rule lets you flip a conditional probability — say, finding the odds a patient is sick given a positive test. What is it?
Bayes' theorem: Mathematical rule for inverting probabilities.
Members of this warm-blooded class range from the 5.5 cm bee hummingbird to the 2.8 m ostrich, share toothless beaked jaws, and lay hard-shelled eggs — what are they?
Bird: Warm-blooded animals with wings and feathers.
Holding the title of smallest great ape, this creature has pinker lips and a darker face than its close cousin, and was once dismissed as merely a 'pygmy' subspecies of it — what is it?
Bonobo: Species of great ape. Taxonomically, members of the chimpanzee/bonobo subtribe Panina—composed entirely by the genus Pan—are collectively termed panins.
Nicknamed 'the lawyer' and 'freshwater cod,' this coldwater fish is the only member of its genus and the sole freshwater species in its entire order — what fish is it?
Burbot: Species of fish. The species is closely related to marine fish such as the common ling and cusk, all of which belong to the family Lotidae (rocklings).
Also known as Flinders rose, this perennial shrub with rounded fleshy leaves and white-to-pink flowers is native across circum-Mediterranean countries — what's the plant called?
Marketed as a COX-2 inhibitor, this NSAID treats arthritis pain and menstrual cramps but carries heart attack and stroke risk warnings — which drug?

This antibiotic is used as an eye ointment for conjunctivitis and, when safer options fail, to treat meningitis, plague, cholera, and typhoid — but in newborns it can trigger a dangerous swelling condition called gray baby syndrome — what drug is it?
Chloramphenicol: Antibiotic. Chloramphenicol is an antibiotic useful for the treatment of a number of bacterial infections.
Also known as a trefoil for its three-part leaves, this legume has been farmed for over 1,000 years to fix nitrogen in soil, and a rare four-leaf version is considered a good-luck charm — what plant?
This medium-to-large sea snail's shell tapers to a noticeable point at both ends thanks to its high spire and siphonal canal — what type of shelled creature is it?
Conch: Shell or sea snails. Conch (US: KONK, KONCH, UK: KONCH) is any of a number of different medium-to-large-sized sea snails.
Usually viral and often worse at night, this childhood respiratory infection swells the trachea and announces itself with an unmistakable barking, brassy cough — what's it called?
Croup: Respiratory infection often caused by a virus.

Nicknamed the 'Wooden Wonder' for its mostly-timber airframe, this WWII British warplane was among the fastest operational aircraft of 1941 and later moonlighted as a high-speed courier for a national airline — what was it?
De Havilland Mosquito: British multi-role combat aircraft of WW2.
This category of mental health conditions involves an unconscious defense mechanism that fragments consciousness, memory, and identity to protect against traumatic stress — what is it called?
Dissociative disorder: Set of mental health conditions.
A pregnancy complication where the embryo attaches outside the uterus, classically presenting with abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding. What is this condition?
Ectopic pregnancy: Female reproductive system health issue.
In this concept, a random variable's average uncertainty is measured by how much data is needed, on average, to describe which outcome occurred. What is this quantity called?

Entropy (information theory): Average uncertainty in variable's states. The choice of base for 
 
 
 
 log
 
 
 {\displaystyle \log }, the logarithm, varies for different applications.
With a cinnamon body, black-and-white wings, and a tall erectile crest, this widespread bird announces itself with a soft 'oop-oop-oop' call — what is it?
Eurasian hoopoe: Species of bird. The Eurasian hoopoe or common hoopoe (Upupa epops) is the most widespread species of hoopoe.
This Swiss thinker, alongside Charles Sanders Peirce, is considered one of the two founders of semiotics — the field he himself called 'semiology' — who is he?
Ferdinand de Saussure: Swiss linguist and philosopher (1857–1913)
With a bushy tail, triangular ears, and a reputation for cunning that echoes through folklore worldwide, which small omnivorous canid lives on every continent except Antarctica?
Also known as the Indian bison, this Vulnerable-listed bovine is the largest living member of the wild cattle family, with most of its roughly 21,000 individuals found in India — what animal is it?
Gaur: Largest species of the bovid family.

A colorless, sweet-tasting, syrupy liquid, this sugar alcohol carries three hydroxyl groups, forms the backbone of triglycerides in fats and oils, and doubles as a food-industry sweetener. What is it?

Once nearly all lumped into a single genus before 21st-century research proved that grouping polyphyletic, these grey-and-white seabirds have an older dialect name, 'mew,' echoing their calls — which birds?
Gull: Subfamily of seabirds. The large species take up to four years to attain full adult plumage, but two years is typical for small gulls.
This medical term describes red blood cells rupturing and spilling their contents into the plasma — a process triggered by bacterial toxins or even intense exercise. What is it?
Hemolysis: Rupturing of red blood cells and release of their contents. Hemolysis may occur in vivo or in vitro.
Often called the founder of alpinism and modern meteorology, this Genevan scientist is also credited with building the first successful solar oven — who was he?
Horace Bénédict de Saussure: Genevan scientist and mountaineer (1740–1799)
Marked by dizziness, blurred vision, and fatigue, this cardiovascular condition is generally diagnosed when systolic readings fall under 90 mmHg — what is it?
This ring-shaped structure in the eye controls how much light reaches the retina by adjusting the size of the pupil — and it's also what determines eye color — what is it?
Iris (anatomy): Colored part of an eye.
Once a deputy district attorney in Weld County, Colorado, this now-suspended lawyer served on Donald Trump's 2020 campaign legal team — who is she?
A genus of roughly 125 succulent species native mostly to Madagascar, one of its members became one of the first plants ever sent into space, aboard a Soviet resupply mission in 1979 — which genus?
Kalanchoe: Genus of flowering plants in the stonecrop family.
Named from Greek words for 'hare' and 'form,' this mammalian order splits into rabbits-and-hares on one branch and pikas on the other, totaling around 110 living species — which order?
Also sold as Xylocaine, this amino-amide local anesthetic numbs in minutes and doubles as a treatment for dangerous ventricular heart rhythms — what is it?
Lidocaine: Local anesthetic. Lidocaine, also known as lignocaine and sold under the brand name Xylocaine among others, is a local anesthetic of the amino amide type.

Credited as a 'Father of Cinematography,' this French artist filmed the Roundhay Garden Scene in Leeds in 1888 — then vanished without a trace two years later, and his work never shaped commercial cinema. Who was he?
Louis Le Prince: French motion-picture pioneer (1841–1890s)
Distinguished from living elephants by spirally twisted tusks and a thick coat of fur for cold climates, this extinct genus survived from the late Miocene until roughly 4,000 years ago — what was it?
Mammoth: Extinct genus of mammals. The oldest mammoth representative, Mammuthus subplanifrons, appeared around 6 million years ago during the late Miocene in southern and Eastern Africa.

Marked by small white Koplik spots inside the mouth and a red rash that starts on the face before spreading, this highly contagious, vaccine-preventable disease can bring fevers over 40°C — which disease?
Despite little formal schooling, this self-taught English scientist uncovered the principles behind electromagnetic induction and established the concept of the electromagnetic field — who is he?
Michael Faraday: English chemist and physicist (1791–1867)
Discovered in 1778 by Carl Wilhelm Scheele and boasting the sixth-highest melting point of any element, this metal is mostly used in steel alloys — what is it?
Molybdenum: Chemical element with atomic number 42 (Mo)

It strikes when blood flow to the heart muscle stops, killing tissue — classically a crushing chest pain that radiates to the left arm or jaw, though women more often feel only neck pain or fatigue. What is this medical emergency?
Myocardial infarction: Interruption of cardiac blood supply.
A vitamer of vitamin B3 that the body can build from tryptophan, in large prescription doses it lowers LDL and raises "good" HDL cholesterol — what's this compound also called niacin?
Nicotinic acid: Organic compound and a form of vitamin B3.

With atomic number 118, this synthetic element boasts the highest atomic number and mass of any known element, and was named to honor the physicist who led the hunt for the periodic table's heaviest members — what is it?
Oganesson: Chemical element with atomic number 118 (Og)

Powered by NADH and FADH₂ handed off from glycolysis and the citric acid cycle, this mitochondrial pathway is how nearly all aerobic organisms produce ATP — far more efficiently than fermentation. What's it called?
Oxidative phosphorylation: Metabolic pathway. Oxidative phosphorylation uses these molecules and O2 to produce ATP, which is used throughout the cell whenever energy is needed.
Nicknamed the empress tree for its fast growth and showy foxglove-like blooms, which East Asian hardwood has become an invasive species across the Eastern US?
Paulownia tomentosa: Species of deciduous tree classified in its own family.
Turning colorless in acid and a fuchsia pink in base, this phthalein dye is a favorite indicator for acid-base titrations — what is it?
Phenolphthalein: pH indicator that turns pink in basic solution.
Widely planted along London's streets as a hybrid variety, this tree genus includes the sycamores of North America and can tower up to 50 meters — which genus?
Platanus: Genus of flowering plants constituting the family Platanaceae.
What is this — “Medical condition where an erection lasts excessively long”?
Priapism: Medical condition where an erection lasts excessively long. Priapism is a condition in which a penis remains erect for hours in the absence of stimulation or after stimulation has ended.
Usually caused by E. coli spreading up the urinary tract, this kidney infection typically brings fever and flank tenderness, and can be prevented by urinating after sex — what condition is it?
Pyelonephritis: Inflammation of the kidney. It is typically due to a bacterial infection, most commonly Escherichia coli.

Named after a 19th-century British naturalist employed by the East India Company, this small deer species native to south-eastern China and Taiwan has also become an established wild population in the UK and Ireland — what is it?
Reeves's muntjac: Species of deer. It has also been introduced in the United Kingdom, Ireland, the Netherlands, Belgium, and Japan.
Grown in South Africa's Fynbos biome, this caffeine-free herbal infusion has an earthy flavor similar to yerba mate and carries protected designation of origin status in the EU. What is it?
Rooibos: Species of plant in the family Fabaceae.

This Harvard political scientist coordinated security planning for Jimmy Carter's National Security Council, but he's best remembered for a 1993 theory arguing future wars would be fought between cultures rather than countries — who was he?
Samuel P. Huntington: American political scientist and academic (1927–2008)
This secretive Soviet chief designer built the rocket that launched the first satellite, the first animal in orbit, and the first human into space — who was he?
Lose your coiled shell entirely and you're called a slug; keep one big enough to retract into and you're this shelled gastropod instead — what creature?
